structured_output.summary: The change implements parseFloat as the spec describes. It calls ToString, then TrimString with start, then finds the longest StrDecimalLiteral prefix and converts it. I checked these cases by reading the code: sign handling, -0, Infinity, a lone ".", "1.", ".5", "1.e5", incomplete exponents, and NaN when no prefix matches. The gate shows 108 of 108 target tests passing with no regressions. The only edit is to parse_float.rs, plus an import of the existing trim_string helper. One minor point: `.parse::<f64>().unwrap_or(f64::NAN)` is a defensive fallback that cannot be reached, because the formatted string is always a valid float literal.
